How research priority works

Within qualified setups and developing leads, stocks with a Positive or Strong buyer track record rank first, then catalyst recency and shared buying. A historical score never replaces the evidence checks.

These are research candidates, not buy instructions or win probabilities. A qualifying setup needs a published thesis with two evidence families and a primary source, a dated catalyst within the past seven days, confirmation and invalidation conditions, at least one Positive or Strong buyer and a stock/ADR or call-option purchase with no later compatible sale in loaded history, current price history and at least $1m of estimated latest-session stock turnover. Challenged, mixed, inconclusive or invalidated reviews cannot qualify. No review means follow-up pending.

Ranked by usable historical track-record score, then newest catalyst and distinct households. More buyers do not prove coordination or expected gains. Unknown data blocks qualification. Older purchases can qualify when a new catalyst appears. Coverage is incomplete; no later disclosed sale does not prove a position is still held. Options may have expired; all option-related returns shown here refer to the underlying stock.

Swing context

Indicator definitions

Simple moving averages use completed closes. RSI and ATR use 14-session Wilder smoothing. ATR measures range, not direction. Volume compares the last session with the preceding 20. Relative performance is the stock’s price return minus SPY’s over identical dates; dividends are excluded. The prior 20-session high uses closes and excludes the latest session. Indicators describe history and are not entry recommendations.

ATR · RSI
S&P 500 · SPY price proxy indexed to first common close
Position planner · Quote currency

Whole shares, in the quote currency. Stop fills are not guaranteed; gaps, slippage, fees and short borrow costs can increase losses. Short losses can be unlimited. Plans are saved on this device.

Tracked politicians. Coverage includes historical outperformers and research candidates. Inclusion is not a buy recommendation. Compare returns available after public disclosure.

Equal-weight completed holding windows. After-disclosure entry uses the first close strictly after the public date. Win = positive price return. Stocks, ADRs and ETFs only; options excluded. Missing data stays unscored.

Method & coverage

One observation per politician, ticker and purchase date; repeated ownership rows count once. Excludes options, exercises, sales and local imports. Period filters purchase dates. After-disclosure entry uses the first available daily close strictly after the public date; purchase basis uses the exact trade-day close. Exit is 5, 20 or 60 subsequent closing observations later; incomplete windows are excluded. Median reporting delay uses all eligible dated purchases. Drawdown is the worst peak-to-trough decline in any scored window, using daily closes, not intraday lows or a combined portfolio. SPY comparison requires identical entry/exit dates. Repeated ticker/date ownership rows count once; overlapping windows are not independent samples. No dividends, fees, taxes, execution slippage or sale matching. Prices and disclosure coverage can be incomplete. Annual estimates do not determine these rankings.

Connecting to feeds…

poor checks feeds on opening, on returning to the tab and every 15 minutes while visible. Disclosure feeds are cached for 6 hours; price data for 15 minutes. Refreshing runs on the hosted website. A six-hour research collector also runs while the configured PC is awake and its user is signed in; Home shows the last report.

Last successful feeds are saved on the server. Errors trigger a 10-minute retry cooldown. A source check is not proof that the publisher released new filings. The Congress feed scans up to 5,000 latest rows from the last 365 days and retains only the nine tracked households, plus their historical seed records. Executive feeds are no longer displayed. Existing checked records take precedence when a feed covers the same document, person, ticker and date. Feed summaries are not independently verified; corrections rely on the providers.

Sources: CongressInvests · Open Cabinet · Yahoo Finance.

Imports

Price gain / loss

Yahoo Finance daily closes refresh automatically; the close date is shown on each row. The offline fallback was fetched September 26, 2026. Since trade = (latest close ÷ trade-day close − 1) × 100. Since disclosure uses the disclosed-day close instead. If that date or price is missing, the value is unavailable; no nearby trading date is silently substituted. Close prices are split-adjusted; dividends, fees and taxes are excluded. No intraday execution price is assumed. Options show the underlying stock change, not option returns; exercises use the exercise-day close, not the strike. This is a hypothetical holding-period price change, not verified politician profit or the return available after public disclosure. Price-source links and dates are in each trade. Missing data and sales display a dash. New price histories cover up to two years. Older or unresolved transactions may have no comparable price.

Shared buying flags

At least two distinct politician households purchasing the same ticker within the selected 7–90 day span, based on trade dates. Stocks, ADRs and calls count; sales, exercises, ETFs and other assets do not. Repeat trades and spouse/joint purchases count once per politician. Flags are ranked by buyer count, then newest trade date. Counts use all available feed households, including those outside the featured list, excluding user imports; table filters do not change them.

Each window’s first and last trade must fit the span; overlapping windows can appear separately. These are historical patterns in incomplete, delayed disclosures, not live alerts or a probability of insider information. Flags recalculate when new disclosures are loaded.

Read the dates and ownership

The disclosure gap counts calendar days from trade to the disclosed date. Congressional rows use their reported filing date; exact release times are unavailable. Executive signatures are labeled separately from publication dates. When publication is unknown, poor shows “Not supplied” instead of treating the signature as disclosure. This gap is not a legal lateness determination. Covered transactions generally must be reported within 30 days of notification and no later than 45 days after the transaction. Amounts are reported brackets, not execution prices or profits. Spouse, joint and self ownership remain distinct. Options and exercises are labeled separately from ordinary stock purchases.
